luke: Quick flag — after the kernel-selection tweak in abc1234 we're seeing 3x tail latency on small (<=4) batch requests in staging. GPU traces (nsys) look unchanged, but CPU-side perf/flame shows a hotspot in the batching/scheduler path. repro + perf data attached: https://perf.example/1999998888 :thinking:

sankar: can you paste the perf script snippet or perf top output? curious if it's syscall/futex or a hot Python frame. :eyes:

luke: pasted quick perf script stack from a 60s record (collapsed stack excerpt):
```
batcher_thread
  batching::Batcher::enqueue
  batching::Dispatch::push
  runtime::KVCache::maybe_evict
  std::mutex::lock
  __lll_lock_wait
  futex_wait
```
Seems like runtime::KVCache::maybe_evict is running under the same mutex used by the batcher enqueue path. eviction runs occasionally but it's pulling other work into hot path.

maria: ugh — we merged the kv-eviction patch that runs eviction synchronously inside the insert lock (commit def4567). That explains it: eviction path can do a bit of work (scanning slab). For small batches the enqueue latency is dominated by that lock.

ben: quick experiment idea — try a try_lock fastpath / lock-free enqueue and fall back to mutex only if contested. cheap patch:```cpp
// fastpath
if (mu_.try_lock()) {
  enqueue_slow();
  mu_.unlock();
} else {
  fallback_enqueue();
}
```
Also run `perf record -g -F 250 -p <pid> -- sleep 30` to get better callgraphs.

luke: ran two variants in staging: (1) baseline (abc1234) and (2) try_lock fastpath. Results (p50/p95/p99 of small-batch latency):
- baseline: 12ms / 185ms / 420ms
- try_lock fastpath: 11ms / 72ms / 110ms
Significant improvement on tails. No throughput regression.

maria: nice. can you drop a short diff/PR and include a microbenchmark? also check the KV-cache correctness under concurrent eviction (race surface).

luke: opened draft PR: https://git.internal/rw/runtime/pull/4523 — includes microbench and perf traces. One oddity: p99 for medium batches (<=32) went up slightly (~+8ms). digging into perf shows an extra branch in enqueue for lock-free fallback that sometimes costs more when highly contended.

ben: maybe expose a tunable: prefer_trylock=true for latency-sensitive tenants and disable for bulk workloads. also think about moving eviction to background worker to decouple entirely.

perf-bot: perf-regression-checker — CI profile for PR 4523 shows: kernel_user_ticks delta +0.4%, syscalls (futex) -12%, user-space lock contention -37%. cc @sankar @maria

sankar: thanks everyone. next steps: (1) land try_lock fastpath behind flag, (2) schedule KV eviction background worker spike work, (3) add e2e toggles for tenant-level opt-in. I'll follow up with a design doc for eviction backgrounder. :thumbsup:
